sentences.text: This computational study investigated transitions between reactant and product states using molecular dynamics simulations, identifying the committor function as a key metric that calculates the probability of a system reaching a product state before returning to a reactant state. The authors noted that learning this function is difficult because of the high dimensionality of the molecular configuration space.

To address this, researchers proposed a new method using a loss function derived from Itō's formula to train a neural network for approximating the committor function. They compared the new approach against existing methods using the Müller-Brown potential as a test case and introduced a strategy that couples their method with Adaptive Multilevel Splitting to improve the sampling of reactive trajectories.

The proposed methodology requires only the initial knowledge of reactant and product states to iteratively learn the committor function, offering a streamlined computational framework for analyzing complex molecular transitions.
